title: The balance sweep
notes: Upgrades: higher levels cost more, climbing steadily so the top ones take a few days to save for. The first few levels cost the same as before, and levels you already have stay.
changes: Battle Tower: type boosters (Charcoal, Mystic Water and the rest) stack up to 3, like the Expert Belt.
Bench healers now heal at most a quarter of your lead’s HP every 3 turns.
Friend battles: both trainers’ Pokémon now pick their moves the same way.
Drizzle, Drought, Sand Stream and Snow Warning weather lasts 5 turns, like the games.
Raids keep their current battle rules for now.
fixes: Battle fixes: Rocky Helmet only hurts a Pokémon that touches it with an attack.
Battle fixes: Venoshock and Barb Barrage only double their power against a poisoned Pokémon (Venoshock did four times the damage).
Battle fixes: Truant (Slaking), Slow Start (Regigigas) and Defeatist (Archeops) now work.
Battle fixes: a Void Pokémon’s Shadow Veil halves a hit it survives. It no longer brings back a Pokémon that was knocked out.
Battle fixes: Spicy Extract raises the target’s Attack and lowers its Defense, like the games.
Battle fixes: after Glaive Rush, attacks on its user can’t miss and do double damage until it moves again.
Battle fixes: Crafty Shield only blocks status moves, Quick Guard only priority moves and Wide Guard only moves that hit everyone.
Battle fixes: Disguise, Intrepid Sword and Dauntless Shield work once a battle, and Shedinja always has 1 HP.
Battle Tower: a Mega Evolution keeps its run stats (it got stronger than it should).
Battle Tower bosses: Rough Skin, Iron Barbs, Aftermath, Rocky Helmet, sandstorms and trapping moves hurt one HP bar at a time.
Battle Tower: the run page fits the Events window without scrolling, on the desktop and on phones.

title: The Battle Tower update: Hard Mode
notes: Battle Tower Hard Mode: a Nuzlocke climb for trainers whose best Climb reached floor 150. Bring one of your own Pokémon. Any Pokémon that faints in Hard Mode is gone for good: the one you bring and every one you catch.

Hard Mode rules: no Revives and no Rest Stops (a small heal after every boss), and closing the game or loading a backup won’t bring a fainted Pokémon back. The rules show before every run. Hard Mode needs a connection.
Hard Mode foes are much tougher: they grow twice as fast as the Climb’s, with extra stats on top.

Hard Mode pays for the risk: everyone still standing comes home with you, catches included (put a catch in the box to keep it safe). Rare looks are twice as likely as in the Climb, Gilded four times, and run prizes are doubled.
Every week (Monday to Sunday, UTC), your first Hard Mode climb past floor 75 earns a Nature Mint of your choice, and past floor 100 a Bottle Cap.
Tower battles have a new look: every battle shows its floor and island, Dens are dark with a glow around the Den’s Pokémon, and bosses get their own stage with HP bars you can see break.
My odds: a new button next to Help at the top of the Day Care shows your own odds for rare looks (your route, eggs, the Battle Tower and Hard Mode) and the hatch odds of the pair in the pen.
changes: Battle Tower (Climb, Daily and Hard Mode): catching is much easier, about 3 times the odds you’d have on your route and far more for Legendaries, and Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Spectral and Gilded Pokémon are no harder to catch than plain ones.

Tower and island bosses: healing moves, status damage and Super Fang-style moves now work on one HP bar at a time, like raid bosses (a boss could heal its whole HP pool, and one Super Fang took several bars).
Supporters can now switch their name effect off in Settings.
fixes: A Tower boss caught with a Master Ball can now be traded and sold like any other catch.
Browser: no more blank screen after an update — the page refreshes itself.

title: Rare Candies with your account
notes: Rare Candies are now kept with your account, so they're safe on every device.
